transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Support, what do you need.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi, I'm looking at my bill and I'm being charged for a premium package I never signed up for, it's an extra forty dollars.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, what's the account.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And what's the charge exactly.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It says 'Premium Sports Tier', forty dollars, I've never watched a sports channel in my life.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Sometimes those get added during promotions.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I never agreed to any promotion though.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It happens automatically sometimes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That doesn't sound right, can you actually look into why it's on my account?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I mean it's just there, not much to look into really.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Something doesn't just appear on a bill for no reason.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Stuff happens, systems aren't perfect.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: When exactly did this charge start showing up, do you have a date?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Says it started last billing cycle.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So about a month then. Is there any note on the account about why it was added?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Nothing specific showing here.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That seems like something that should be logged somewhere.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Not always, depends on how it got added.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you at least tell me if it was something I clicked, or something added on your end?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Hard to say from here honestly.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's a pretty important thing not to know.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I just see what's on the screen, not the whole history.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is there someone who can see the whole history then?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Maybe billing, again.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Everything keeps going back to billing.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's kind of their department, yeah.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Are there any other charges on my account I should double check while we're at it?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I mean I could read the whole bill to you if you want.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That would actually be helpful, yes.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Internet service, standard fee, premium sports tier forty dollars, equipment rental, taxes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, equipment rental? I own my own router.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Says rental here.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's another charge I never agreed to then.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I mean it's just what the system shows.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So there might be two incorrect charges now, not just one.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Could be, not really my area to dig into why.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: This is starting to feel like a pattern, not just one mistake.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I couldn't really say either way.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you at least remove the equipment rental charge too?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can note it, same as the other one, but the removal and refund would still be a billing thing.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So essentially you can't actually fix anything on this call.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can note things, that's about it from here.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you remove it and refund the charge?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can remove it going forward, refunds are a separate process.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So I just lose the forty dollars for something I never asked for?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's kind of how it works unless you dispute it separately.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am disputing it, right now, with you.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can't personally issue refunds from this screen.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Then who can?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Billing department, different queue.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: This is genuinely frustrating, I've been on hold for twenty minutes already before you even picked up.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yeah call volume's high today.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's not really addressing what I said.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What do you want me to say.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Some acknowledgment that this is a real problem would be nice.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Look, I hear you, but I can't do much more than remove it going forward.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you at least transfer me to billing then, without me having to call back and wait again?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Transfers can take a while too, might be faster to just call back.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That seems like a really unhelpful answer honestly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's just the reality of how the queues work.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Has this happened to other customers too, or is it just me?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No idea, I don't track that.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It would be useful context if this is a known bug versus just my account.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I really wouldn't know either way.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is there anyone who would know that?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Maybe a manager, maybe not even them honestly.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: This whole call just keeps circling back to 'I don't know'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's kind of what I've got today.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you check if my account has any credits available at least, for the inconvenience?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Not something I can apply from here.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Who can apply that then?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Probably billing, or a supervisor maybe.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Everything keeps needing someone else.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's just how it's split up here.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you send me something in writing confirming these two charges are disputed, at least?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can add a note, not sure it generates anything you'd actually get emailed.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So I wouldn't even have proof this conversation happened.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: There'd be a call log internally, just not something sent to you necessarily.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's not very reassuring.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's just how the system's set up.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is there a way to escalate this formally, like a case number or ticket?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Might generate one automatically, I'm not totally sure.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You don't seem sure about much on this call.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I've answered what I can.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is there a supervisor I could speak to about this instead?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: They're going to tell you the same thing I'm telling you.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'd still like to ask, that's my right as a customer.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Sure, I can flag it, don't expect a fast response though.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, so nothing's actually getting resolved on this call.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I removed the charge going forward, that's something.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Forty dollars I never agreed to is still just gone though.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I already told you that's a billing thing.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You keep saying that like it's my fault for asking.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I didn't say that.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It kind of feels that way honestly, the way you're talking to me.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm just telling you how it is, not much else I can do about the tone.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You could at least sound like you care a little.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I've got a lot of calls today, not really the priority right now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wow, okay. That's a pretty bad thing to say to a paying customer.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's just honest.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can we please just focus on fixing this instead of you being dismissive?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I removed the charge, told you how to get the refund, what more do you want.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Some basic courtesy would be a start.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I don't really have time for a lecture on customer service right now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: This is exactly the kind of thing that makes people cancel their service entirely.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Look, I've told you three times already what to do about the refund, if you don't like the answer, feel free to get lost and try a competitor.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Excuse me? That is completely unacceptable, I want your name and a supervisor right now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's Blake, and like I said, someone will get back to you eventually.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: This has been one of the worst customer service experiences I've ever had.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Noted. Anything else.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, I'm done, I'll be filing a complaint about this entire call.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Do what you need to do.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Unbelievable.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I want it on record that I was told to get lost by a support agent over a billing error.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's on record, whatever that's worth to you.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It should be worth quite a lot, honestly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Sure. Anything else.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yep.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net.
